title: Boundaries, Confidentiality & Digital Conduct
summary: Understand professional boundaries, confidentiality, responsible device use, social media considerations, and appropriate use of workplace systems.
objectives: Identify common professional boundaries in workplace relationships and systems.
Explain why confidential or restricted information must be protected.
Apply responsible judgment to devices, social media, photos, recordings, and workplace technology.

vocab.def: Protecting information that should only be accessed or shared by authorized people for appropriate purposes.
A limit that defines appropriate behavior, responsibility, access, or relationships in a workplace setting.
Permission to access information, systems, locations, or resources for an approved purpose.
Responsible use of devices, accounts, communication tools, social media, and workplace technology.

sections.heading: Access should match your role
sections.body: Having the technical ability to open a file, enter an area, or use a system does not automatically mean you are authorized to do so. Professional workers use information and systems only for legitimate work purposes within granted access.

sections.heading: Confidential information must be protected
sections.body: Depending on the workplace, protected information may include customer data, health information, financial details, employee records, business plans, security information, or internal communications.

sections.heading: Personal devices can create workplace risks
sections.body: Phones, cameras, recordings, messaging apps, and personal cloud accounts may create privacy, security, safety, or distraction concerns. Workers should learn the actual policy before taking photos, recording, transferring files, or using personal devices.

sections.heading: Social media does not erase workplace responsibility
sections.body: Posting workplace information, images, customer details, coworker information, or internal events can create serious problems even when posted from a personal account. Confidentiality and workplace policies still matter.

practice.prompt: You can technically access a folder that is unrelated to your job responsibilities. Should you open it out of curiosity?
practice.answer: No. Access should be based on legitimate work purpose and authorization, not curiosity.

practice.prompt: You want to take a photo at work and post it online. What should you consider first?
practice.answer: Workplace policy, privacy, confidentiality, security, safety, and whether photography or posting is authorized.

quiz.question: Which statement best reflects professional digital conduct?
options: Use workplace systems and information only for authorized, appropriate purposes
Anything visible on a workplace system can be shared
Personal social media is completely separate from workplace confidentiality
If a device belongs to you, workplace rules never apply to how it is used at work
quiz.answer: Use workplace systems and information only for authorized, appropriate purposes

lab.objective: Analyze scenarios involving devices, social media, confidentiality, system access, photos, and professional boundaries.

reflectionPrompt: Why can having technical access to information be different from having professional authorization to use it?

evidenceCandidate.title: Professional Boundaries and Digital Conduct Scenario Analysis
